lessons.title: Linguistic diversity and dialects
lessons.anelcac: Notions of linguistic diversity, dialects, names of languages, geographical classification
objectives: Becoming aware of the linguistic diversity of Cameroon (about 280 languages according to the LACAGEO Mini-Atlas)
Distinguish language, dialect and variant according to academic definitions
Naming Fe'fe' and locating it in the geographical classification of the languages of Cameroon
Adopt an attitude of respect towards all languages

teacher.intro: Lesson: Linguistic diversity and dialects. Module: Module I — Cameroonian linguistic diversity.
steps: **Setting the context:** Display the map of the Linguistic Mini-Atlas of Cameroon. Ask students which languages are spoken in their family.
**Exploration:** Have students read the definitions in the Mini-Atlas (language, dialect, patois, national language). Locate Fe'fe' in its linguistic region.
**Conceptualisation:** Explain the language / dialect distinction with examples: the Bulu, Ewondo, Eton and Mangisa dialects all belong to the Beti-Fang language (Mini-Atlas).
**Application:** Complete a table: name of the language, family, main region, ISO code.
**Assessment:** Each student gives an oral presentation of Fe'fe', indicating family and region.
teacher.freedom: The LACAGEO Mini-Atlas (2013) distinguishes about 280 living languages in Cameroon. The exact number varies according to the criteria (SIL: 274, Ethnologue: 279). Value all the languages cited.
teacher.tips: The LACAGEO Mini-Atlas (2013) distinguishes about 280 living languages in Cameroon. The exact number varies according to the criteria (SIL: 274, Ethnologue: 279). Value all the languages cited.

student.intro: Cameroon is one of the richest nations in the world in languages — the linguistic Mini-Atlas lists about 280! In this lesson, you discover the place of Fe'fe' in this great family.
activities: Look at the Mini-Atlas map and find the area where Fe'fe' is mainly spoken.
Copy and complete: Fe'fe' belongs to the ___ family. It is mostly spoken in the ___ region.
According to the Mini-Atlas, how many living languages are there in the Fe'fe' region? Note down this number.
Survey: ask an adult the name of the language in which they were raised and where it is spoken.
Memorise: **dialect** = an intelligible variant of the same language; **national language** = language of an ethnic group that does not extend beyond the borders of one State (ACA LAN).
student.memo: Cameroon has about **280 languages** according to the LACAGEO Mini-Atlas. Fe'fe' belongs to a Cameroonian language family and has its own dialectal variants. According to the ACA LAN, a national language is the language of an ethnic group that does not extend beyond the borders of one State.

lessons.title: Classification of languages and linguistic atlas
lessons.anelcac: Classification of the languages of Cameroon: linguistic areas, families, ALCAM atlas
objectives: Name the main linguistic areas of Cameroon
Read and interpret an extract from a linguistic atlas (ALCAM / Mini-Atlas)
Classify Fe'fe' according to its typological criteria
Producing a short text presenting Fe'fe'

teacher.intro: Lesson: Classification of languages and linguistic atlas. Module: Module I — Cameroonian linguistic diversity.
steps: **Setting the context:** Go back over the definitions. How many language families do students remember?
**Presentation:** The 8 world language families according to Ethnologue (Niger-Kordofanian, Nilo-Saharan, Afro-Asiatic…). Place Cameroonian languages within this whole.
**Explanation:** Show how to find Fe'fe' in the ALCAM: ISO code, family, location.
**Guided practice:** In pairs, students find 3 languages neighbouring Fe'fe' and note their ISO codes.
**Production:** 5-line paragraph presenting Fe'fe' (family, region, speakers, distinctive feature).
teacher.freedom: The online ALCAM is on the Mozilla Data Collective. The LACAGEO Mini-Atlas covers all the administrative regions with maps and statistics.
teacher.tips: The online ALCAM is on the Mozilla Data Collective. The LACAGEO Mini-Atlas covers all the administrative regions with maps and statistics.

student.intro: A linguistic atlas is a specialised map. The ALCAM (Atlas of the Languages of Cameroon) and the LACAGEO Mini-Atlas let you locate Fe'fe' precisely.
activities: On the Mini-Atlas map, locate Fe'fe' and note its administrative region.
List 3 languages whose area is adjacent to that of Fe'fe'.
Classify these 4 languages in a table: Language | Family | Main region.
Write an introductory paragraph about Fe'fe' with at least 5 pieces of information taken from the atlas.
Memorise: **ISO 639** = international language codes; **ALCAM** = Atlas des Langues du Cameroun.
student.memo: The **ALCAM** and the **LACAGEO Mini-Atlas** list and locate all the national languages of Cameroon. Cameroon has 8 main language families. Fe'fe' appears there with its family and its location. Knowing how to read a linguistic atlas is reading the history of peoples.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module II — Segmental phonology: vowels and consonants
lessons.title: Vowels of Fe'fe'
lessons.anelcac: AGLC vowels — simple, specific, complex
objectives: Identify the simple vowels of the phonological system of Fe'fe'
Recognising specific vowels absent from French
Pronouncing vowels correctly in the context of a word
Transcribing words containing vowels according to AGLC

teacher.intro: Lesson: Fe'fe' vowels. Module: Module II — Segmental phonology: vowels and consonants.
steps: **Setting the context:** Write known words in Fe'fe' on the board and ask which sounds students hear.
**Presentation:** Introduce the AGLC. Write the simple vowels of Fe'fe' on the board, articulating them clearly.
**Explanation:** Vowels specific to Fe'fe' that are absent from French (nasal, particular openness…). Listening and repetition exercises.
**Application:** List of 10 words — students underline the vowels and indicate: simple or specific.
**Assessment:** Dictation of 5 simple words — students transcribe them with the correct vowels.
teacher.freedom: Use the examples from the platform's ALCAM vocabulary. For each specific vowel, give a memorable key word.
teacher.tips: Use the examples from the platform's ALCAM vocabulary. For each specific vowel, give a memorable key word.

student.intro: Every language has its own sounds. In Fe'fe', some vowels do not exist in French. This lesson teaches you to hear, pronounce and write them.
activities: Listen to the recordings of the Fe'fe' vocabulary and identify the vowels you hear.
Classify the vowels: **Shared with French** | **Specific to Fe'fe'**.
Transcribe the 5 dictated words, taking care to note each vowel correctly.
Find 3 words in Fe'fe' for each specific vowel and write them down.
Memorise: **AGLC** = Alphabet Général des Langues Camerounaises, the official reference.
student.memo: The vowel system of **Fe'fe'** includes simple vowels and specific vowels (e.g. nasalised vowels). They are written using the **AGLC**. Mastery of vowels is the basis of reading and writing in Fe'fe'.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module II — Segmental phonology: vowels and consonants
lessons.title: Fe'fe' consonants and written production
lessons.anelcac: Consonants — simple, specific, complex; written production of vowels and consonants
objectives: Identify the consonant system of Fe'fe'
Recognising specific consonants absent from French
Articulate consonants correctly in context
Writing words with vowels and consonants correctly notated

teacher.intro: Lesson: Fe'fe' consonants and written production. Module: Module II — Segmental phonology: vowels and consonants.
steps: **Setting the context:** Recall the vowels. What is a consonant?
**Presentation:** Table of Fe'fe' consonants according to the AGLC. Stress the specific consonants (labio-velars, prenasalised, implosives…).
**Explanation:** Articulating difficult consonants: in isolation → syllable → word.
**Application:** Minimal pairs: listening to words that differ only by one consonant.
**Production:** 5 simple sentences in Fe'fe' with careful consonant transcription.
teacher.freedom: Implosive and prenasalised consonants are often the most difficult for students who learned to read and write in French. Repeat the listening activities many times.
teacher.tips: Implosive and prenasalised consonants are often the most difficult for students who learned to read and write in French. Repeat the listening activities many times.

student.intro: After the vowels, here are the consonants of Fe'fe'! Some are unique — you will only hear them in Fe'fe' and in a few neighbouring African languages.
activities: Listen to the minimal pairs and tick the word you hear (e.g. bìlí / pìlí).
Transcribe 5 dictated words, paying attention to the specific consonants.
Find in the vocabulary all the words containing a prenasalised consonant. How many do you find?
Compose 3 simple sentences in Fe'fe', each with at least one specific consonant.
Memorise: **minimal pair** = two words identical except for one phoneme.
student.memo: The consonant system of **Fe'fe'** includes consonants shared with French and specific consonants (implosives, prenasalised, labio-velars…). Writing them according to the **AGLC** is essential for reading and writing.

lessons.title: Definition and functions of tones
lessons.anelcac: Tones — definition, function, presentation; simple tones (high, low, mid)
objectives: Define tone as a distinctive feature of tone languages
Distinguish lexical tone from grammatical tone
Identify the simple tones of Fe'fe'
Transcribing words with their tones according to AGLC

teacher.intro: Lesson: Definition and function of tones. Module: Module III — Suprasegmental phonology: tones.
steps: **Setting the context:** Say two Fe'fe' words that are written the same but have different tones and different meanings.
**Presentation:** Define tone. Present the simple tones of Fe'fe' and their AGLC diacritics.
**Explanation:** Simple tones: high (´), low (`), mid (¯). Have students repeat each tone.
**Application:** Match recorded words with their tone notation.
**Assessment:** Dictation of 5 words — students note the tones.
teacher.freedom: Singing the tones helps to memorise them. Use a flute or whistle the tonal melodies.
teacher.tips: Singing the tones helps to memorise them. Use a flute or whistle the tonal melodies.

student.intro: Fe'fe' is a tonal language: the pitch of your voice changes the meaning of the word! You will learn to hear and write down these tones.
activities: Listen to the pairs of words. For each pair, are the tones the same or different?
Transcribe 5 words with their tones using the AGLC diacritics (´ ` ¯).
Find 2 words in the vocabulary that differ only in tone. What does each one mean?
Sing the tones of a 3-syllable word as High-Low-High, then Low-High-Low. What difference do you hear?
Memorise: high tone = ´ ; low tone = ` ; mid tone = ¯.
student.memo: In **Fe'fe'**, tone is phonological: it distinguishes words with different meanings. The **simple tones** are high (´), low (`), and sometimes mid (¯). They are written using the **AGLC** diacritics.

lessons.title: Complex tones and tone-marked written production
lessons.anelcac: Complex tones (rising, falling); finding the tone of a word; tonal written production
objectives: Identify the complex tones of Fe'fe' (rising, falling)
Finding the tone of a word by the isolation method
Transcribing sentences with full tone marking
Producing a short text in Fe'fe' with correct tones

teacher.intro: Lesson: Complex tones and tonal written production. Module: Module III — Suprasegmental phonology: tones.
steps: **Setting the context:** Recall the simple tones. Announce that some syllables carry two tones in succession.
**Presentation:** Complex tones: falling (̂), rising (̌). Let students hear them and reproduce them.
**Explanation:** Isolation method: say the word with an artificial high tone, then a low one, and listen to which sounds natural.
**Application:** Students find the tone of 10 words in Fe'fe' using the isolation method.
**Production:** Dialogue of 6 lines in Fe'fe' with complete tone notation.
teacher.freedom: The complex falling tone is often the most frequent. Start with it before the rising tone.
teacher.tips: The complex falling tone is often the most frequent. Start with it before the rising tone.

student.intro: You know the simple tones. Now for the complex tones of Fe'fe' — syllables that rise and fall at the same time!
activities: Listen to the recorded words and sort them: Simple tone | Complex tone.
Apply the isolation method to 5 words: say them high, then low, and note the tone you perceive.
Transcribe a dialogue of 4 lines in Fe'fe' with all the tones marked.
Write a 3-sentence text in Fe'fe' about an action from your daily life, with tone marking.
Memorise: falling tone = ̂ ; rising tone = ̌.
student.memo: The **complex tones** of **Fe'fe'** (falling ̂, rising ̌) are melodic movements on a single syllable. The **isolation method** makes it possible to find the tone of an unknown word. A transcription in Fe'fe' without tones is incomplete.

lessons.title: The noun base and noun classes
lessons.anelcac: NP: constituents, base noun + affixes, noun classes, personal pronouns
objectives: Identify the structure of the noun in Fe'fe' (base + affixes)
Recognising the noun classes of Fe'fe'
Form the singular and plural of nouns
Use the personal pronouns corresponding to noun classes

teacher.intro: Lesson: The noun base and noun classes. Module: Module IV — The noun phrase.
steps: **Setting the context:** Write a noun in Fe'fe' in the singular and plural. What changes?
**Presentation:** Noun class: in Bantu and Bantoid languages, nouns are grouped into classes marked by prefixes.
**Explanation:** Main noun classes of Fe'fe' with singular and plural prefixes.
**Application:** Table: singular → plural for 10 nouns.
**Assessment:** Identify the noun class of 5 nouns.
teacher.freedom: Start from the nouns that students already use. Noun classes often correspond to semantic categories (humans, animals, objects…).
teacher.tips: Start from the nouns that students already use. Noun classes often correspond to semantic categories (humans, animals, objects…).

student.intro: In Fe'fe', nouns are organised into **classes**. Each class has its own prefixes for the singular and plural — a much richer system than gender in French!
activities: Using the Fe'fe' vocabulary, make a table: Singular | Plural | Noun class.
Identify the class prefix in each noun. Highlight it.
Put the following 5 nouns into the plural by changing the prefix according to the class.
Match each noun with its corresponding class pronoun.
Memorise: **noun class** = grammatical category of nouns, marked by prefixes.
student.memo: In **Fe'fe'**, nouns are organised into **noun classes** marked by prefixes. A change of prefix indicates number. Pronouns, adjectives and verbs agree with the class of the noun.

lessons.title: Noun determiners
lessons.anelcac: Determiners: possessives, demonstratives, numerals, indefinites, interrogatives; noun class agreement
objectives: Identify the different types of determiners in Fe'fe'
Make determiners agree with the noun according to the noun class
Build complex noun phrases
Producing sentences with complete NPs

teacher.intro: Lesson: Noun determiners. Module: Module IV — The noun phrase.
steps: **Setting the context:** Write a simple noun phrase. How can it be enriched?
**Presentation:** Determiners in Fe'fe': possessives, demonstratives, numerals, indefinites, interrogatives.
**Explanation:** Each determiner agrees with the class of the noun (same class prefix or suffix).
**Application:** Complete noun phrases with the correct determiner according to the class.
**Production:** 5 complex noun phrases (noun + 2 determiners) used in sentences.
teacher.freedom: Stress class agreement — one of the most distinctive features of Fe'fe' compared with French.
teacher.tips: Stress class agreement — one of the most distinctive features of Fe'fe' compared with French.

student.intro: A noun with its determiners becomes much more precise! In Fe'fe', determiners agree with the **noun class**.
activities: Complete the NPs with the correct possessive determiner according to the noun class.
Underline the determiners in 5 sentences in Fe'fe' and identify their type.
Turn each simple noun phrase into a complex noun phrase by adding a demonstrative and a numeral.
Write 5 sentences in Fe'fe' with at least two determiners per noun phrase.
Memorise: **class agreement** = the determiner changes form according to the noun class.
student.memo: In **Fe'fe'**, all determiners (possessives, demonstratives, numerals, indefinites, interrogatives) agree with the **noun class** of the noun. A **complex NP** = noun + nominal base + agreeing determiners.

lessons.title: The verb stem and conjugation
lessons.anelcac: VP: constituents, stem, affixes, conjugation, verb tenses
objectives: Identify the verb stem and the conjugation affixes in Fe'fe'
Conjugate a verb in the main tenses
Analyse the morphological structure of a verb form
Use verb forms correctly in sentences

teacher.intro: Lesson: The verb stem and conjugation. Module: Module V — The verb phrase.
steps: **Setting the context:** Write a verb form in Fe'fe' and ask students to identify the stem.
**Presentation:** Break down a verb form: subject prefix + TAM markers + stem + suffixes.
**Explanation:** Conjugation paradigm of a common verb in Fe'fe' in several tenses.
**Application:** Conjugation table: 3 common verbs.
**Assessment:** Translate 5 sentences from French into Fe'fe'.
teacher.freedom: The TAM system of Fe'fe' is often richer than that of French. Start with the most commonly used tenses.
teacher.tips: The TAM system of Fe'fe' is often richer than that of French. Start with the most commonly used tenses.

student.intro: The verb is the heart of the sentence in Fe'fe'. It alone carries tense, aspect, mood and subject! In this lesson, you take apart the verbal mechanics.
activities: Break down 5 verb forms in Fe'fe': subject prefix | TAM marker | stem | suffix.
Conjugate the verb 'to eat' in Fe'fe' in 3 different tenses for all persons.
Identify the tense of 5 sentences in Fe'fe' and justify your answer.
Translate 3 sentences from French into Fe'fe', taking care with the conjugation.
Memorise: **TAM** = Tense-Aspect-Mood; this is what verbal affixes express in Fe'fe'.
student.memo: In **Fe'fe'**, a verb form = subject prefix + TAM markers + stem + suffixes. The **TAM** (Tense-Aspect-Mood) system expresses more precise temporal and aspectual nuances than in French.

lessons.title: Verbal moods and negation
lessons.anelcac: Moods: indicative, imperative; negation; written production of simple/complex VP
objectives: Identify and use the main verbal moods of Fe'fe'
Form the verbal negation
Build simple and complex verb phrases
Producing a text with a variety of moods and aspects

teacher.intro: Lesson: Verbal moods and negation. Module: Module V — The verb phrase.
steps: **Setting the context:** Give an order in Fe'fe'. Which mood is used?
**Presentation:** Moods in Fe'fe': indicative, imperative, and other aspectual moods.
**Explanation:** Formation of the negative in Fe'fe': prefix, negative suffix, or particle.
**Application:** Turn 5 affirmative sentences into negative ones and vice versa.
**Production:** 8-sentence text alternating affirmation, negation and imperative.
teacher.freedom: Negation in Fe'fe' can be double (framing the verb) or simple. Show both cases.
teacher.tips: Negation in Fe'fe' can be double (framing the verb) or simple. Show both cases.

student.intro: Giving an order, expressing doubt, denying an action — each nuance has its own form in Fe'fe'!
activities: Put the 5 given sentences into the negative form.
Turn these 5 statements into imperatives addressed to a friend.
Identify the mood and polarity (affirmative/negative) of each sentence in the text provided.
Write a dialogue of 6 lines including at least 2 imperatives and 2 negations.
Memorise: **mood** = the way of viewing the action; **negation** = grammatical marker denying the action.
student.memo: In **Fe'fe'**, the main moods are the **indicative** and the **imperative**. **Negation** is marked by a particle or a specific affix. The diversity of moods is an expressive richness of Fe'fe'.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module VI — The sentence in Fe'fe'
lessons.title: The simple sentence and its types
lessons.anelcac: Simple, interrogative, negative and imperative sentence; word order
objectives: Analyse the structure of the simple sentence in Fe'fe'
Distinguish the 4 types of sentences
Mastering the order of constituents
Producing varied simple sentences

teacher.intro: Lesson: The simple sentence and its types. Module: Module VI — The sentence in Fe'fe'.
steps: **Setting the context:** Read a sentence in Fe'fe'. Who does what?
**Presentation:** Basic constituent order in Fe'fe'. Compare with French.
**Explanation:** The 4 sentence types from the same basic sentence.
**Application:** Turn declarative sentences into interrogative ones, then into negative ones.
**Production:** 8 varied sentences (2 per type) about school life.
teacher.freedom: Word order in Fe'fe' may differ from French. This is a typological feature, not a mistake.
teacher.tips: Word order in Fe'fe' may differ from French. This is a typological feature, not a mistake.

student.intro: A well-constructed sentence in Fe'fe' follows precise rules. You learn the types of sentences and word order.
activities: Identify the order of constituents in 5 sentences in Fe'fe'.
Turn 4 declarative sentences into yes/no questions.
Turn these 4 sentences into negatives.
Write 2 sentences of each type (declarative, interrogative, negative, imperative).
Memorise: the basic order in **Fe'fe'** is typologically stable.
student.memo: The **simple sentence** in **Fe'fe'** has a characteristic order of constituents. The 4 types (declarative, interrogative, negative, imperative) are formed with specific grammatical markers.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module VI — The sentence in Fe'fe'
lessons.title: Logical connectors and the complex sentence
lessons.anelcac: Logical connectors, complex sentence, coordination, subordination; written production
objectives: Identify the logical connectors of Fe'fe'
Distinguish coordination from subordination
Build complex sentences
Producing a coherent text with syntactic variety

teacher.intro: Lesson: Logical connectors and the complex sentence. Module: Module VI — The sentence in Fe'fe'.
steps: **Setting the context:** Read a short story in Fe'fe'. Which words link the sentences?
**Presentation:** Connectors in Fe'fe': coordinating and subordinating conjunctions.
**Explanation:** Complex sentence by coordination / by subordination. Examples in Fe'fe'.
**Application:** Link 5 pairs of simple sentences with the appropriate connector.
**Production:** 10-sentence text on 'A day in my village' with 5 different connectors.
teacher.freedom: The connectors of Fe'fe' often have French equivalents but with different syntactic positions.
teacher.tips: The connectors of Fe'fe' often have French equivalents but with different syntactic positions.

student.intro: To tell stories and argue, you need to link your sentences. The **logical connectors** of Fe'fe' are your tools!
activities: Underline all the connectors in the text provided.
Classify them: Addition | Cause | Consequence | Opposition | Time.
Link 5 pairs of sentences with the most appropriate connector.
Write a text of 8 sentences with at least 4 different connectors.
Memorise: coordination = same level; subordination = one sentence inside another.
student.memo: In **Fe'fe'**, **logical connectors** make it possible to build coherent **complex sentences**. Varying syntactic structures improves the quality of written and spoken expression.

lessons.title: Greeting, introducing yourself and interacting in Fe'fe'
lessons.anelcac: Everyday communication situations: greetings, introductions, polite expressions
objectives: Mastering greeting formulas according to context
Introducing yourself and someone else in Fe'fe'
Use polite and respectful expressions
Holding a short everyday conversation

teacher.intro: Lesson: Greeting, introducing yourself and interacting in Fe'fe'. Module: Module VII — Everyday life (Level 1).
steps: **Setting the context:** Two students meet at the market. Act out the scene in French, then ask how to say it in Fe'fe'.
**Presentation:** Greetings in Fe'fe' according to the time of day, age and context.
**Explanation:** Formulas of respect towards elders, specific to Fe'fe' culture.
**Role play:** In groups of 2, simulate encounters in various contexts (market, school, ceremony).
**Production:** Dialogue of 10 lines between two people of different generations.
teacher.freedom: Greeting rules reflect deep cultural values. Value the knowledge of students from families who speak the language.
teacher.tips: Greeting rules reflect deep cultural values. Value the knowledge of students from families who speak the language.

student.intro: Knowing how to greet in Fe'fe' means respecting the culture! The greetings change depending on whom you greet and at what time.
activities: Complete the table of Fe'fe' greetings: Time | Formula | Expected response.
Play role A: greeting an elder at the morning market.
Make up a dialogue of 8 lines between a child and their grandfather.
Note down 3 Fe'fe' politeness formulas with no direct equivalent in French.
Memorise the morning and evening greeting formulas, and those for elders, in Fe'fe'.
student.memo: **Greetings** in **Fe'fe'** vary according to the time of day, status and social context. They reflect the community's values of respect and solidarity.

lessons.title: Express everyday needs and actions
lessons.anelcac: Real-life situations: shopping, requests for help, travelling, daily activities
objectives: Express everyday needs in Fe'fe'
Describe daily activities
Use vocabulary for places and actions of everyday life
Producing a descriptive text on a typical day

teacher.intro: Lesson: Expressing everyday needs and actions. Module: Module VII — Everyday life (Level 1).
steps: **Setting the context:** Images of scenes from daily life — market, field, school, home. How can they be described in Fe'fe'?
**Presentation:** Thematic vocabulary: food, travel, household activities.
**Simulation:** Market scene: buyer and seller in Fe'fe'.
**Application:** Describe your day in Fe'fe' (from waking up to going to bed).
**Production:** 10-sentence text: 'My day in Fe'fe''.
teacher.freedom: Everyday vocabulary is the most motivating. Link the ALCAM words to real situations.
teacher.tips: Everyday vocabulary is the most motivating. Link the ALCAM words to real situations.

student.intro: You know how to greet people. Now you are going to manage in everyday situations in Fe'fe': at the market, on the road, at home.
activities: Match each picture of a scene from daily life with the corresponding word or sentence in Fe'fe'.
Play the role of the seller at the market: answer the requests in Fe'fe'.
Write 5 sentences describing your morning activities from the time you wake up.
Translate these 5 sentences about daily journeys into Fe'fe'.
Memorise 10 everyday words in Fe'fe' with their French translation.
student.memo: The **everyday** vocabulary in **Fe'fe'** covers food, getting around and household activities. Mastering it allows functional communication in all contexts.

lessons.title: Argue and persuade in Fe'fe'
lessons.anelcac: Elaborate communication: argumentation, narration, formal speech
objectives: Build a simple argument in Fe'fe'
Use the expressions of formal speech
Narrating a past event coherently
Delivering a 2-minute oral speech in Fe'fe'

teacher.intro: Lesson: Arguing and persuading in Fe'fe'. Module: Module VIII — Everyday life (Level 2).
steps: **Setting the context:** Read a proverb in Fe'fe'. Ask students to explain it and defend it.
**Presentation:** Formulas of formal oral speech in Fe'fe': forms of address, opening, closing.
**Explanation:** Structure of an argument: thesis → arguments → examples → conclusion.
**Practice:** Debate: for or against the use of Fe'fe' at school? Each group defends its position.
**Production:** 2-minute speech on a given theme.
teacher.freedom: Public speaking is highly valued in Cameroonian cultures. Draw on this tradition to motivate the students.
teacher.tips: Public speaking is highly valued in Cameroonian cultures. Draw on this tradition to motivate the students.

student.intro: In Fe'fe' cultures, well-spoken words are a force. You learn to argue and persuade with eloquence.
activities: Identify in the text: thesis, arguments, examples.
Prepare 3 arguments to defend the teaching of Fe'fe' in primary school.
Give an opening speech for a ceremony in Fe'fe'.
Narration: tell in Fe'fe' about a memorable event from your school life.
Memorise the opening and closing formulas of a formal speech in Fe'fe'.
student.memo: **Argumentation** in **Fe'fe'** follows this pattern: thesis → arguments → examples → conclusion. **Formal speech** follows precise cultural conventions. Mastery of elaborate oral expression is a high-level skill.

lessons.title: Oral literature and advanced written production
lessons.anelcac: Oral literature: proverbs, tales, riddles; long written production
objectives: Analyse the structure of a tale or a riddle in Fe'fe'
Identify the themes and values conveyed
Writing a short tale following the conventions of the genre
Using oral literature as a teaching resource

teacher.intro: Lesson: Oral literature and advanced written production. Module: Module VIII — Everyday life (Level 2).
steps: **Setting the context:** Tell or play a short tale in Fe'fe'.
**Presentation:** Genres of oral literature: tales, proverbs, riddles, epics.
**Analysis:** Structure of the tale: initial situation → disruption → events → resolution → moral.
**Application:** Analyse a tale provided, following this structure.
**Production:** Tale of at least 15 lines in Fe'fe' with an explicit moral.
teacher.freedom: Oral literature is a threatened cultural treasure. Invite community storytellers if possible.
teacher.tips: Oral literature is a threatened cultural treasure. Invite community storytellers if possible.

student.intro: Fe'fe' tales, proverbs and riddles are literary works in their own right. You will analyse them and you will create your own!
activities: Read the tale provided and identify the 5 stages of its narrative structure.
Identify 3 moral values taught by this tale.
Translate a proverb in Fe'fe' into French and explain its figurative meaning.
Write a short tale (15 lines) in Fe'fe' with a moral about work or respect.
Memorise: tale = fictional narrative with an educational purpose; proverb = brief formula of collective wisdom.
student.memo: The **oral literature** of **Fe'fe'** (tales, proverbs, riddles) transmits the values of the community. The tale has a 5-stage structure. Writing it in Fe'fe' draws on all the language skills acquired.

lessons.title: Who are the Fondjenti (Ntî)? Identity, language and territory
lessons.anelcac: Cultural areas, cultural identity, settlement
objectives: Name the Fondjenti (Ntî) community and explain its name
Locating your territory and its neighbours
Telling one's origin according to tradition
lessons.competence: Introduce the Fondjenti (Ntî) community (name, language, territory, neighbours, origin) and place it within the cultural diversity of Cameroon.
lessons.situation: A pen pal from another region asks you to introduce the Fondjenti (Ntî) community to them: who are they, where do they live, where did they come from?
lessons.materiel: Map of Cameroon, cultural profile of the community (“Cultures” section of Likalo).

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Present the Fondjenti (Ntî) community (name, language, territory, neighbours, origin) and place it within the cultural diversity of Cameroon.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read aloud: “A pen friend from another region asks you to introduce the Fondjenti community (Ntî): who are they, where do they live, where do they come from?” Students think individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — What do the Fondjenti (Ntî) call themselves and what does this name mean? — What language do they speak, and where else is it spoken? — Which peoples do they live with? — Where did they come from, according to tradition?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present the following elements, or have the students discover them: • The group brings together the Ntî who came from Bamwa, the Fondonti who came from the north and the Bapoutchis, the first occupants, as well as the Bakou; the Fondonti princes are the most numerous. • Everyone speaks Nufi fluently. • A very open and expansive group, proud of its exogamy: wives are found there from the North, from Beti country and elsewhere. • These are lands of conquest. After independence, unrest displaced the group, which is returning to the ancestors' lands for its sacred places. • Having come from Bamwa, Fondjomokwet and Fondonti, the Ntî remain tied to Bamwa: it is a chief of Bamwa who enthrones the chief of Bapougueu.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: The Fondjenti chiefdom brings together Ntî from Bamwa, the Fondonti and the Bapoutchis found on the spot; all speak Nufi. A dynastic monarchy, deliberating brotherhoods, skull worship and the sacred place of the palm, “the tree that gives everything”, characterise this people, proud of their exogamy and hospitality.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: On a map of Cameroon, locate the Fondjenti (Ntî) community and its neighbours, then write 5 sentences to introduce it to your pen pal.

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

teacher.freedom: Some knowledge (rites, sacred places, initiate societies) is restricted: in class, only what the community makes public is covered, with respect and without judgement. Compare with the students' own culture.
teacher.tips: Approach recommended by the National Cultures teaching guide: active and participatory methods (“learning by doing”). If possible, invite a resource person from the community, or propose a survey of the elders.

lessons.title: Power and social organisation among the Fondjenti (Ntî)
lessons.anelcac: Socio-political organisation, rules for living together
objectives: Identify traditional authorities
Explain how decisions are made
Identifying the rules of deference
lessons.competence: Describe how the Fondjenti (Ntî) organise power, make decisions and regulate community life.
lessons.situation: An important decision has to be made for the whole Fondjenti village (Ntî). Who decides, and how?
lessons.materiel: The community's cultural profile, paper and felt-tip pens for the organisation chart.

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Describe how the Fondjenti (Ntî) organise power, make decisions and regulate community life.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read out: “An important decision has to be made for the whole village of the Fondjenti (Ntî). Who decides, and how?” The students think about it individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — Who holds authority? — How are decisions made (consensus, vote, the chief's decision)? — What rules of respect and deference are observed? — Which groups or societies play a particular role?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present, or have the students discover, the following: • Dynastic monarchy: major decisions emerge from debate in three brotherhoods, until consensus; the chief promulgates them. • No prohibitions between the sexes, but certain places are closed to women, except those who hold a title of notability. • To maintain peace, wives are exchanged between allied peoples. • The group has always included supporters of the conquest of new territories.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: Dynastic kingship: major decisions arise from debate in three brotherhoods, until consensus is reached; the chief then promulgates them. There are no taboos between the sexes, but certain places are closed to women, except those who hold a title of notability. To maintain peace, wives are exchanged between allied peoples.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: Draw a diagram (organisation chart) of power among the Fondjenti (Ntî), then explain in 3 sentences how a decision is made.

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

teacher.freedom: Some knowledge (rites, sacred places, initiate societies) is restricted: in class, only what the community makes public is covered, with respect and without judgement. Compare with the students' own culture.
teacher.tips: Approach recommended by the National Cultures teaching guide: active and participatory methods (“learning by doing”). If possible, invite a resource person from the community, or propose a survey of the elders.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module C-II — Cultural practices: ways of life
lessons.title: Traditional food and drink of the Fondjenti (Ntî)
lessons.anelcac: Ways of life: culinary practices
objectives: Naming traditional foods and drinks
Describe a preparation
Linking food to the living environment
lessons.competence: Identify the traditional dishes and drinks of the Fondjenti (Ntî), describe how they are prepared and bring out their cultural significance.
lessons.situation: Your class is preparing a food fair. Your group must present a traditional dish of the Fondjenti (Ntî).
lessons.materiel: Cultural profile, pictures or local ingredients, display materials.

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Identify the traditional dishes and drinks of the Fondjenti (Ntî), describe how they are prepared and draw out their cultural significance.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read aloud: “Your class is preparing a food fair. Your group must present a traditional dish of the Fondjenti (Ntî).” Students think individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — What are the main dishes and drinks? — What products are they made from? Where do these products come from? — Who prepares them, and on what occasions? — What do they say about the community's living environment?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present, or have the students discover, the following: • Traditional dishes: kwa kuku, koki, taro (pé), mbyətʃʉ sauce (giant frogs). • Drinks: palm wine. • Men: farming, especially the palm tree, from which everything is drawn and which they refuse to cut down, and hunting. Women: fields, and fishing for giant frogs and tadpoles for the mbyətʃʉ sauce.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: The Fondjenti (Ntî) eat mainly kwa kuku, koki, pé, mbyətʃʉ sauce. Traditional drinks: palm wine. These dishes are linked to the group's activities and to the products of its environment.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: Choose a dish of the Fondjenti (Ntî): write its sheet (name in the language, ingredients, steps, occasion when it is served).

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module C-II — Cultural practices: ways of life
lessons.title: Clothing, adornments and crafts of the Fondjenti (Ntî)
lessons.anelcac: Ways of life: clothing practices, crafts
objectives: Describe traditional clothing
Identify craft objects and their use
Explain the criteria of beauty
lessons.competence: Describe the clothing, adornments and craft objects of the Fondjenti (Ntî), and explain their use and value.
lessons.situation: A museum asks you to prepare a display on the clothing and crafts of the Fondjenti (Ntî).
lessons.materiel: Cultural profile, craft objects or photos of craft objects, recycled materials.

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Describe the clothing, adornments and craft objects of the Fondjenti (Ntî), and explain their use and value.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read out: “A museum asks you to prepare a display case on the clothing and crafts of the Fondjenti (Ntî).” The students think about it individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — How did people dress in the past, and how do they dress today? — Do clothes indicate status or occasion? — What objects are made, from what materials, and for what uses? — What are the criteria of beauty?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present the following elements, or have the students discover them: • The ndzí ndɔ is the only traditional outfit that marks identity; women wear the wrapper. • Seduction: formerly being a good warrior; today knowing how to dance and make people laugh; for a woman, an outfit that shows off her figure. • Basketry (baskets, sleeping mats) and weaving (bags, roofing mats), disappearing for lack of transmission. • Beauty: physique in men; in women, a fine figure, formerly enhanced with red padauk powder.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: The ndzí ndɔ is the only traditional dress that marks identity; women wear the wrapper. Attractiveness: formerly being a good warrior; today knowing how to dance and make people laugh; for a woman, an outfit that shows off her figure. Basketry (baskets, sleeping mats) and weaving (bags, roofing mats), disappearing for lack of transmission.

lessons.title: Birth, name and the passage to adulthood among the Fondjenti (Ntî)
lessons.anelcac: Key events: birth, naming, initiation
objectives: Explain the meaning of a birth
Describe how names are given
Describe the passage to adulthood
lessons.competence: Explain how the Fondjenti (Ntî) welcome a child, give them a name and mark their entry into adulthood.
lessons.situation: A child has just been born into a Fondjenti (Ntî) family. How will he or she be named, and how will he or she become an adult?

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Explain how the Fondjenti (Ntî) welcome a child, give them a name and mark their entry into adulthood.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read aloud: “A child has just been born into a Fondjenti family (Ntî). How will the child be named, and how will they become an adult?” Students think individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — What does a birth mean for the community? — Who gives the name, when and how? — Can the name change during a lifetime? — When and how does one become a man or a woman?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present, or have the students discover, the following: • Names in ma- (mafeu) are feminine, those in ta- (tafeu) masculine. • It is the father who names the child, and family history is passed on through the name; it is changed only once, very rarely, to ward off bad luck. • Notables are addressed by their title. • Birth is a reincarnation; death is the passage to a spiritual life from which one protects one's own, who appear in dreams. • A boy becomes a man when he knows how to build his hut and his father gives him a wife; a girl, when she marries.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: Names in ma- (mafeu) are feminine, those in ta- (tafeu) masculine. It is the father who names the child, and family history is passed on through the name; a name is changed only once, very rarely, to ward off bad luck. Notables are addressed by their title.

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

lessons.title: Marriage and bride price among the Fondjenti (Ntî)
lessons.anelcac: Key events: marriage
objectives: Putting the stages of marriage in order
Explain the symbolism of the bride price
Comparing yesterday and today
lessons.competence: Describe the stages of traditional Fondjenti (Ntî) marriage, the bride price items and their symbolism.
lessons.situation: Your elder brother wants to marry a young Fondjenti (Ntî) woman. Which steps will he have to follow?
lessons.materiel: Cultural profile, props for the staging.

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Describe the stages of the traditional Fondjenti (Ntî) marriage, the elements of the bride price and their symbolism.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read aloud: “Your older brother wants to marry a young Fondjenti woman (Ntî). Which steps will he have to follow?” Students think individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — Who chooses the spouse? Do people marry within the group or outside it? — What are the stages of marriage? — What does the bride price include, and what does each item symbolise? — Where does the couple live after the marriage?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present, or have the students discover, the following: • Patrilineal kinship, formerly matrilineal with widespread polygamy; after the negotiations of the young man's parents, the woman settles in his family. • The boy becomes a man when he knows how to build his hut and his father gives him a wife; the girl, when she marries. • Stages: meeting, informing the father, “knocking at the door”, unofficial introduction, information on what must be brought, bride price, marriage contract. • Bride price: goat, wrappers, oil, meat, wine, money, kola, palm wine. The number of lobes of the broken kola is interpreted, and white wine seals the pact.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module C-IV — Cultural practices in communities (Level I)
lessons.title: Leisure: traditional music and dances of the Fondjenti (Ntî)
lessons.anelcac: Community practices: leisure, traditional dances
objectives: Identify dances and their occasions

lessons.situation: Taking part in cultural life in the family and in society: the class prepares a Fondjenti (Ntî) dance performance for the cultural day.
lessons.materiel: Instruments or recordings, costumes, clear space.

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Identify the traditional dances of the Fondjenti (Ntî), choose the most representative one, describe it, draw out its cultural significance and act it out.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read aloud: “Participation in cultural life in the family and in society: the class is preparing a Fondjenti dance performance (Ntî) for the cultural day.” Students think individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — Which dances are practised, and on what occasions? — Who dances (men, women, children, initiates)? When and where? — Which instruments, songs and outfits are used? — What is the cultural meaning of the chosen dance?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present, or have the students discover, the following: • Rhythms: ndàndzì (large and small tam-tam), kù'ŋgàʔ, ndzéʔ ntʃàʔ, ŋkùæ (two slit drums), ŋgùmèlɔŋ. • The kù'ŋgàʔ and the ndzéʔ ntʃàʔ are initiates' dances; the ŋkʉæ and the ŋgùmèlɔŋ are open to all. • The zɨŋ, a major ceremony, may be organised by the chief, once or several times per reign, to honour his deceased father or mother.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: Among the Fondjenti (Ntî), the traditional dances (kù'ŋgàʔ, ŋkʉæ) accompany the major moments of life: festivals, mourning, weddings, initiations. Instruments: tam-tams, slit drums. Festival(s): zɨŋ.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: Describe a dance of the Fondjenti (Ntî) (participants, time, instruments, gestures, meaning), then perform it with your group.

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

objectives: Identify economic activities
Explain the division of tasks
Explain access to land
lessons.competence: Describe the economic activities of the Fondjenti (Ntî), the division of tasks between men and women and the rules of access to land.
lessons.situation: A development project wants to help the Fondjenti (Ntî). First you need to understand how they work and who owns the land.

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Describe the economic activities of the Fondjenti (Ntî), the division of tasks between men and women and the rules of access to land.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read out: “A development project wants to help the Fondjenti (Ntî). First, we need to understand how they work and who owns the land.” The students think about it individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — What are the activities of men? of women? — Who owns the land and how is it accessed? — Which products are sold or exchanged? — Have these activities changed?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present the following elements, or have the students discover them: • Men: farming, especially the palm tree, from which everything is drawn and which they refuse to cut down, and hunting. Women: fields, and fishing for giant frogs and tadpoles for the mbyətʃʉ sauce. • Land belongs to men; it is not sold but given, with pride in settling people around oneself. • Basketry (baskets, sleeping mats) and weaving (bags, roofing mats), disappearing for lack of transmission.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: Men: farming, especially the oil palm, from which everything is obtained and which people refuse to cut down, and hunting. Women: fields, and fishing for giant frogs and tadpoles for the mbyətʃʉ sauce. Land belongs to men; it is not sold but given, with pride in settling people around oneself.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module C-V — Cultural practices in communities (Level II)
lessons.title: Beliefs, sacred places and taboos among the Fondjenti (Ntî)
lessons.anelcac: Community practices: symbolism, rites, taboos
objectives: Explain beliefs about life and death
Identify sacred places
Explain the role of taboos
lessons.competence: Explain the beliefs, sacred places and taboos of the Fondjenti (Ntî), and their role in regulating social life.
lessons.situation: A visitor arrives among the Fondjenti (Ntî). Which places and rules must they absolutely respect?

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Explain the beliefs, sacred places and taboos of the Fondjenti (Ntî), and their role in regulating social life.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read out: “A visitor arrives among the Fondjenti (Ntî). What places and rules must they absolutely respect?” The students think about it individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — What are the beliefs about birth and death? — Which places are sacred, and why? — What are the main taboos, and for whom? — How were serious offences atoned for?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present the following elements, or have the students discover them: • Ancestor worship: their relics (skulls) are kept and people come to ask them for protection and blessing. • Every family has its house of skulls (dzʉtʃú), the first sacred place of the compound, and its zʉʔsié, “place of the gods of the compound”; the fæk, at the chiefdom, is a mystical corridor linking each large compound to the palace. These places are often marked by a large tree. • Birth is a reincarnation; death is the passage to a spiritual life from which the dead protect their own, who are visited by them in dreams. • Taboos: abortion, prostitution. Women do not farm on sacred days; some notables do not share their plate on those days. • Courting the chief's wife was the supreme offence.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: Ancestor worship: their relics (skulls) are kept and people come to ask them for protection and blessing. Each family has its skull house (dzʉtʃú), the first sacred place of the compound, and its zʉʔsié, “place of the gods of the compound”; the fæk, at the chiefdom, is a mystical corridor linking each large compound to the palace. These places are often marked by a large tree.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: Write a short guide to good conduct for a visitor among the Fondjenti (Ntî) (3 places or rules to respect, with the reason for each).

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module C-V — Cultural practices in communities (Level II)
lessons.title: Greeting, introducing yourself and counting in Nufi
lessons.anelcac: Traditional media and transmission: everyday language
objectives: Greeting according to the time of day
Introducing yourself
Counting from 1 to 10

vocabulary.frenchText: morning greetings (as a sign of deference/respect)

lessons.competence: Use the greeting and introduction formulas of the Fondjenti (Ntî) and count from 1 to 10, respecting customs.
lessons.situation: You are visiting a Fondjenti (Ntî) family. Greet them, introduce yourself and take part in sharing the kola nuts while counting.
lessons.materiel: Cultural profile (“Common expressions” and “Counting” sections), kola nuts or small objects.

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Use the greeting and introduction formulas of the Fondjenti (Ntî) and count from 1 to 10, respecting customs.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read aloud: “You are visiting a Fondjenti family (Ntî). Greet them, introduce yourself and take part in the sharing of the kola nuts by counting.” Students think individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — How do you greet people depending on the time of day? — How do you introduce yourself (name, origin, place of residence)? — How do you count from 1 to 10? Is the system decimal, vigesimal…? — Why is language a tool of transmission?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present the following elements, or have the students discover them: • The language of the community is Nufi. • Greeting formulas: Tʃæ᷅ʔsi = Hello (neutral formula, at any time); Nzoe yi lê = morning greeting (one person); Nzoe yi lê = morning greeting (several people). • Counting from 1 to 5: Nohʉ, Pʉæ, taæ, Kwæ᷅, tî. • The founding ancestor, Fʉəwàŋ (Kuæ Melʉ̀ʔ), is “the handle of the conqueror”. • The palm tree has a special place: it is not cut down, because it gives everything.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: Greeting and counting in Nufi are the first steps towards communicating with the Fondjenti (Ntî). Polite expressions show the respect owed to people according to the time of day and their rank.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: Role play in pairs: greet each other, introduce yourselves, ask where the other person comes from and count objects from 1 to 10.

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

teacher.freedom: Some knowledge (rites, sacred places, initiate societies) is restricted: in class, only what the community makes public is covered, with respect and without judgement. Compare with the students' own culture.
teacher.tips: Approach recommended by the National Cultures teaching guide: active and participatory methods (“learning by doing”). If possible, invite a resource person from the community, or propose a survey of the elders.
